claimText: A Harvard study proved that eating chocolate every day prevents heart disease

brave.title: Harvard study finds cocoa flavanols may benefit heart health
brave.description: A Harvard-led study (COSMOS) found that cocoa flavanol supplements may reduce cardiovascular events, but the results do not mean eating chocolate prevents heart disease.

brave.title: COSMOS trial: Cocoa flavanols and cardiovascular disease — key findings
brave.description: The Cocoa Supplement and Multivitamin Outcomes Study found modest cardiovascular benefits from cocoa flavanol supplements, not from eating chocolate bars.

brave.title: No, eating chocolate every day will not prevent heart disease
brave.description: While cocoa contains flavanols that may support heart health, the American Heart Association cautions against interpreting studies as evidence that chocolate prevents heart disease.

brave.title: Health Check: Does eating chocolate really help your heart?
brave.description: Studies suggest cocoa flavanols have modest benefits, but commercial chocolate products contain high sugar and fat content that may offset any cardiac benefits.

brave.title: Snopes: Claim that Harvard proved chocolate prevents heart disease is misleading
brave.description: Harvard's COSMOS study found benefits from cocoa flavanol supplements, not from eating chocolate. The study's lead researcher explicitly cautioned against this misinterpretation.

factCheck.text: Harvard study proved chocolate prevents heart disease

claimReviewMarkup.title: Misleading: Harvard study was about flavanol supplements, not chocolate
